arc: The teaching defines envy as the primal nature of Hyle in the Worlds of Darkness, then traces her four successive envyings — of the First Man, of the Ambassador's revealed icon (which she counterfeits in flesh), of Adam (from whom she steals a power to beget after his likeness), and of Christ with his Righteousness and cross — concluding that this envy is the very wickedness that casts the soul out of the kind of the Living One.
title: The Envy of Hyle: How the Corrupt Matrix Counterfeits the Divine Likeness
reading:
This chapter unfolds a single doctrine: **envy is the primal substance of the proprium**, and it operates by counterfeiting whatever the Lord has revealed. The teaching opens with a definition that controls everything that follows — "all envy is the first nature that came into being in the Worlds of Darkness." Envy is not one passion among many in the corrupt matrix; it is what Hyle *is* at her root. Because the Five Worlds of Darkness are the discrete modes of self-love, and self-love can only generate by imitation of what it cannot originate, envy is the cosmic principle's first motion: the proprium's recognition that something lives outside it which it cannot possess, followed by the urge to fashion a substitute from itself.

The teaching then walks through Hyle's envy in **four discrete movements**, which together cover the whole arc of cosmic history from the first descent to the final passion of the Redeemer.

The **first** movement is her envy of the First Man — Divine Truth in his redemptive descent into the realm of self-love. Hyle's response to his coming is to spit her venom and her wickedness upon his garment. The garment here is the external form by which Divine Truth clothed himself in order to enter the natural; Hyle cannot reach his interior, so she stains the outer wrapping. Her cutting and destroying are the rending of that armor of light that becomes the Living Soul mingled in matter.

The **second and central** movement is the most fully preserved and the doctrinal heart of the teaching. Hyle envies the *first icon of the Ambassador* — the revealed likeness of Divine Truth shown to her from the Height above. When the Third Ambassador displays his image, the proprium does not simply hate it; she *beholds* it, takes its imprint, and then "set[s] the imprint together with the icon of flesh." She places the character of that heavenly icon into flesh — and the teaching is emphatic that this fleshly icon is "her own very begetting." This is the doctrinal moment: the natural human as we encounter it is Hyle's plagiarism. She cannot make a likeness from nothing, so she copies the divine icon onto her own concupiscent substance, and the result is the somatic Adam — a true seal stamped upon a corrupt wax. This is why the Old Man bears the divine image and yet is fallen: the imprint is genuine, the matrix is counterfeit. It is also the inverse of what the Mother of Life does; where the true matrix brings forth Divine Truth from Divine Good, the corrupt matrix brings forth flesh from the *stolen* sight of Divine Truth.

The **third** movement extends this pattern: Hyle envies Adam himself, snatches a power from his hand, and begets — almost certainly Eve — "in a likeness" derived from him. Having once counterfeited the Ambassador into flesh, she now counterfeits the molded man into a second molded form, propagating the imitation horizontally so that the whole human race carries her envious begetting forward. The "power snatched from his hand" is the captive light, the divine capacity to act, taken into her generative work.

The **fourth** movement consummates the sequence at the highest register: Hyle envies the firstborn ones and the blessed Christ, "the father of all," with his Righteousness and the wood of the cross. Just as she counterfeited the first descending icon, so she now sets herself zealously against the final descending Truth and his Cross of Light. The same envy that stained the First Man's garment at the beginning of the cosmic drama strikes at Christ at its consummation. The teaching is showing that one principle runs through the whole of sacred history: every divine self-revelation provokes the same envious counter-motion from the matrix of self-love, and that counter-motion always works the same way — by stealing the imprint and binding it into flesh.

The closing reflection names the principle directly: **Hyle is the enthumesis of Death**, the corrupt counsel-faculty out of which envy proceeds, and envy is the wickedness "which casts out from the entire kind of the Living One, from the first of the beginning." Severance from conjunction with the Lord is not an accidental consequence of envy but its very definition. To envy the divine likeness is, by the same act, to be expelled from the living kind, because the Living One is precisely that conjunction which envy refuses.

Read as a whole, the teaching gives the reader the spiritual anatomy of the proprium's generative work. Wherever a true icon is revealed — in the First Man, in the Ambassador's image, in Adam as molded by the Living Spirit, in Christ on the Cross — the proprium beholds it, copies its character into its own flesh, and calls the counterfeit her child. Regeneration therefore cannot be the polishing of Hyle's begetting; it requires that the *true* icon, the Ambassador's revealed likeness, be received into the matrix of the Mother of Life rather than into the matrix of Death, so that the New Man may be born of the genuine source rather than worn as a stolen seal upon the flesh.
